findings.title: Imported feed HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html for content supplied by Jobs::PollFeed, and Post#cook returns that raw content verbatim as cooked HTML. The PollFeed path does not pass the content through Readability or any HTML sanitizer, so script elements, event-handler attributes, javascript: URLs, and other active markup from an RSS/Atom item are persisted and later rendered to forum readers. This is a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability if any imported feed item contains malicious or compromised content.

findings.title: Embed URL is interpolated unescaped into raw HTML
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import appends an imported-from footer by interpolating the supplied URL directly into an href attribute and link text. The URL is checked only for an http/https prefix, so a URL containing a single quote or markup can close the attribute or element and inject additional HTML. Because the resulting post uses raw_html cooking, that injected markup is stored and rendered without the normal cooking sanitization.

findings.title: Referer is embedded unescaped in a JavaScript string
findings.body: The embed layout interpolates request.referer directly inside a single-quoted JavaScript string passed to parent.postMessage. A referer containing an apostrophe or crafted path can terminate the string and alter the script executed on the Discourse-origin embed page. The target origin should be derived and serialized safely on the server, for example by extracting the referer's origin and emitting it with proper JavaScript/JSON escaping.

findings.title: Feed polling crashes on items without content
findings.body: poll_feed unconditionally calls i.content.scrub for every feed item. RSS items commonly provide only a description or summary and can therefore have nil content, raising NoMethodError. Because there is no per-item rescue, one such item aborts the entire hourly poll, prevents all remaining items from being imported, and will recur on every run until the feed changes.

findings.title: Unknown embeds enqueue an unbounded retrieval job on every request
findings.body: EmbedController#best enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic whenever no TopicEmbed exists, with no controller-side throttling or deduplication. The 60-second throttle is only checked after a job is dequeued, and the loading page automatically reloads, while non-browser clients can spoof the Referer check trivially. Repeated or malicious requests for a URL that can never be retrieved can therefore flood the Sidekiq queue indefinitely.

findings.title: Remote import fetches arbitrary redirected URLs without timeouts or size limits
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read with no timeout, response-size limit, or validation of the final URI after redirects. TopicRetriever validates only the initial embed_url host, so a page on the embeddable host can redirect the server-side request to another host, including internal services, and a slow or very large response can tie up a background worker or exhaust memory. A bounded HTTP fetch that revalidates redirect targets is needed.

findings.title: Disqus import now depends on live remote pages and aborts on fetch failures
findings.body: The Disqus importer replaces local topic creation with TopicEmbed.import_remote for each thread link. If a link is missing, stale, offline, or returns an HTTP error, open() raises and aborts the whole Thor import, leaving later threads unprocessed; if import_remote returns no post, that thread's Disqus comments are silently skipped. Previously the topic could be created from the export itself, so this change risks losing exported comments solely because the original site is unavailable.

findings.title: Embed controller spec expects synchronous retrieval the controller no longer performs
findings.body: The spec expects TopicRetriever.new and retrieve to be called when no embed exists, but EmbedController#best never references TopicRetriever; it enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic instead. Mocha will report the unmet TopicRetriever expectation, so this test fails and provides no valid coverage of the actual enqueue behavior. The spec should expect the retrieve_topic job enqueue with the user id and embed_url.

findings.title: Protocol-relative URLs are incorrectly rewritten to the source host
findings.body: absolutize_urls treats every href or src beginning with '/' as a path on the source host. Protocol-relative URLs such as //cdn.example.com/image.jpg therefore become http://source-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg instead of retaining the CDN host, breaking external links and images in imported content; the same faulty transformation is applied to img src attributes below. Protocol-relative and ordinary relative URLs need distinct handling.
